pageCache.pageTitle: Old Sarum Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
At Old Sarum Primary, we teach and promote British Values because they help children understand how our country works and how people should treat one another. British Values are part of everyday school life, supporting children to develop respect, responsibility and confidence. We want families to feel reassured that these values are taught in an age-appropriate way that matches our school community and the needs of primary learners.
Our approach includes encouraging children to respect different faiths and beliefs, and to understand that everyone has the right to be listened to. We also support pupils to learn about democracy by practising listening to others, taking turns and contributing ideas in class. Children are taught about the rule of law through clear routines and consistent expectations, helping them understand that rules keep people safe and fair. Through these experiences, pupils learn that their actions have consequences and that they can make positive choices.
British Values also include supporting children to develop tolerance and kindness, especially when they meet differences in people, opinions or backgrounds. We encourage pupils to work collaboratively, celebrate diversity and resolve issues calmly. For parents, this means you can reinforce the same messages at home- talking about fairness, listening to others and encouraging children to be respectful. Together, we can help children grow into thoughtful citizens who contribute positively to their school, community and wider society.

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Sarum Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
At Old Sarum Primary we have whole school collective worship four times a week and class collective worship once a week.
On Monday the assembly is based on Theme of the week which is linked to School and British values.
On Tuesday the assembly is a singing assembly.
On Wednesday the assembly is focused on the OPAL project, with an opportunity to celebrate children's creativity and resilience during play, as well as risk assess future play opportunities.
On Thursday the assembly is class based and we explore global or local community news and issues, using the "Picture News Resource".
On Friday we have a celebration assembly, where we recognise achievements from the week.
Please see the overviews below for more information

pageCache.text:
British Values at Old Sarum Primary School
Old Sarum on the outskirts of Salisbury is a growing vibrant community. Our community Primary School is committed to, and recognises the multi-cultural, multi faith and ever-changing nature of the United Kingdom. We understand the important and vital role we have in ensuring that we promote British Values within all that we do to ensure groups or individuals within the school are not subjected to intimidation or radicalisation by those wishing to unduly, or illegally, influence them.
Our policies and procedures ensure no discrimination against any individual or group, regardless of faith, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, political or financial status, or similar is tolerated. We understand that preparing children for their adult life beyond the curriculum and school is of paramount importance and ensure that we promote and reinforce British values throughout their time with us.
All schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught . The government set out its definition of “British Values” in its 2011 “Prevent Strategy”; These are the values of:
We believe that the best way to promote British values in our school is by example. We aim to embody democracy in the way we work and within the ethos and culture of Old Sarum Primary School. We have a clear and consistent framework of rules, regulations and high expectations which are there for the benefit of us all.

Welcome To Our school
Welcome to Old Sarum Primary School!
It is a privilege and a pleasure to welcome you to our wonderful school community. As the new Headteacher, I am incredibly proud to join a school that sits at the heart of the local community and is built on strong relationships, high aspirations and a genuine commitment to every child's success.
At Old Sarum Primary School, we believe that every child deserves to feel safe, valued and inspired. We are proud of the nurturing environment we provide, where children are encouraged to develop confidence, curiosity and resilience while achieving their very best academically, socially and emotionally.
The strength of our school lies in our people. Our dedicated staff, supportive families, committed governors and, most importantly, our fantastic children work together to create a positive and caring community where everyone is encouraged to flourish. We are also proud to be part of the MLP Trust, whose partnership and collaboration help us to continually grow and improve.
Relationships are at the centre of everything we do. We know that children thrive when home and school work together, and we greatly value the partnership we share with our families. By working closely together, we can ensure that every child receives the very best education and experiences that prepare them for a successful future.
Our school values guide us each day. We encourage everyone in our community to:
These values help us create a culture where children are supported to become thoughtful, responsible and confident learners.
Our vision is simple yet powerful: "A home for the heart, an adventure for the mind and a foundation for the future." We want every child to leave Old Sarum Primary School with wonderful memories, a love of learning and the knowledge, skills and character they need to thrive in the next stage of their education and beyond.
As a parent myself, I understand how important it is to find the right school for your child. Choosing a school is one of the most significant decisions a family makes, and I firmly believe that education has the power to transform lives. I am committed to ensuring that every child at Old Sarum feels happy, challenged and supported to achieve their full potential.
I hope our website gives you a flavour of life at Old Sarum Primary School, but nothing compares to seeing our school in action. I warmly invite you to visit us, meet our staff and children, and experience first-hand the welcoming atmosphere that makes our school such a special place.
I would be delighted to show you around. Please contact the school office to arrange a visit.
I look forward to welcoming you and your family to Old Sarum Primary School.
Polly Bailey Headteacher Old Sarum Primary

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Sarum Primary School - Character Development
pageCache.text:
Character Development
At Old Sarum Primary, we believe strong character development helps children thrive both in and out of the classroom. Alongside teaching reading, writing and maths, we support pupils to build values such as respect, responsibility and kindness. These qualities help children make positive choices, work well with others and learn from mistakes in a safe and encouraging environment.
We focus on practical skills that children can use every day. This includes learning how to manage feelings, listen carefully, take turns and show empathy. Through classroom routines, age-appropriate discussions and consistent expectations, children practise becoming resilient learners. They are encouraged to persevere with challenges and to understand that effort and improvement are part of growing up.
Parents and carers play a vital role in reinforcing these messages at home. We invite families to talk about behaviour, friendships and decision-making using everyday situations, such as school routines, playtime and community activities. If you would like to know more about the specific values and approaches used at Old Sarum Primary, please speak to your child’s class team or contact the school office.

PTA
Old Sarum Primary School Parent Teacher Association (PTA)
Who we are and what we do:
The Old Sarum Primary School PTA is a charity (number: 1201550, https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/charity-search/-/charity-details/5199239) and a group of volunteer parents and teachers who work (hard!) together to put on memorable events for the children and their families, whilst engaging with, and improving relations with the local community. We aim to raise essential funds for purchasing material improvements in the school to enhance the physical school area and learning environment for all who attend. We ran a very successful community summer fête (in July 2024), have funded support for OPAL, author visits and resources to help the children thrive. We run the pre-loved uniform website helping parents save money, shop sustainably and raise funds for the school. We organise fun events and discos throughout the year.
We hold committee meetings informally and use whatsapp to plan and organise future fundraising events. Our Facebook page is here: https://www.facebook.com/OldSarumPrimaryPTA. Find us on Instagram OSP_PTA You can contact us by email pta@oldsarum.wilts.sch.uk.
We are always keen to welcome new people and their ideas for how to raise funds and how they can be spent, to the team (committee or simply event helpers) and would be delighted to hear from anyone that can spare a few hours throughout the year to help. If your company or business is able to offer any help through donations, raffle prizes, volunteering or matched funding please contact us email: pta@oldsarum.wilts.sch.uk.

Matched Funding
Dear Parents and carers,
Do you work for an organisation who has a match funding or match giving scheme? If so, we would love to hear from you. It could be a great way for us to maximise our fundraising. Hundreds of organisations offer match funding schemes, such as banks, building societies, insurance companies, supermarkets, utility providers, phone companies & car manufacturers. Asda, Sainsburys, Tesco & Barclays currently do, or have in the past run such schemes. Many smaller/independent companies may also be interested in match funding. So please do speak to your line manager or human resources department to find out if a donation matching scheme exists. The schemes vary but can include a donation to a charity of your choosing, matching an amount you have donated or matching money you have helped raise whilst volunteering at an event. We assure you we are not asking for any com itment to volunteer or to make a donation and it should be a straightforward process. If for example you were already helping at one of our events, we could double our fundraising efforts. If you think your employer might have a donation scheme, please do get in touch at pta@oldsarum.wilts.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Sarum Primary School - Remote Education
pageCache.text:
Remote Education
If the school has to close due to an unplanned closure then we will provide remote learning.
As a whole school, we will use Parent Mail to maintain contact enabling teachers to share the activities for home learning.
All teachers will be asked to ensure pupils in each of their classes have appropriate work set. This work will be monitored and feedback will be meaningful and given at the appropriate time. Teachers will also be monitoring pupil engagement reporting non-engagement on a regular basis.
Keeping regular learning going during the period that schools are closed is important; however we understand that everyone’s circumstances at home will be different. Some families have one child to support while others have several. Some families have one device to share while others may have more – and some things may work differently on different devices. Some parents will have plenty of time to help their children learn, while others will be working from home and may have much less time and some children will be able to work more independently than others or need greater challenge. If you are worried about any aspect of remote learning then please contact the school office.
